_meta.made: tools-godot/export_models.mjs (lane X1) from the JS game, branch js-final, three r186
_meta.units: JS game world units (a rifleman is about 16 tall, a tank about 40 long). +Y up, the unit FRONT is +X, origin on the ground under the unit centre. Buildings: origin at the footprint centre.
_meta.vertexColours: vertex colours inside the files are sRGB-ENCODED (not linear as glTF says), because Godot keeps vertex colours in 8 bits and linear 8-bit bands the dark paints: set vertex_color_is_srgb = true (x1_models.gd does). Palette colours ("pal") in this manifest are linear like every other colour here.
_meta.colours: every colour here ("c", "e") is LINEAR rgb and may be above 1 (the game brightens some textures); convert to sRGB for a Godot albedo_color
_meta.rigid: a unit/building that is not a squad = "meshes": [{f: shared shape file (one mesh, white material + its texture), p: animated part it belongs to (absent = fixed to the unit root), m: 3x4 matrix (12 numbers, column-major, relative to that part), mat:[per surface {c colour, a alpha, r roughness, mt metalness, e emissive, unlit, ds double-sided, camo/look/refl/wake/trim = runtime shader flags}]}], "parts": {name:{parent, m}} = the nodes the game moves (see partsDoc).
_meta.palette: "pal" on a mesh instance or soldier look = this look's colours for the vertices that differ between nations: in the file those vertices are white with ALPHA = slot/255 (alpha 1 = keep the colour in the file). For every vertex with round(alpha*255) < 255 set its colour to pal[that number] (linear rgb), alpha 1. No "pal" = use the file as it is.
_meta.squad: an infantry kind = "squad": soldier places in the unit frame (x forward, z right) with the look each one wears, "looks": {v0..v3|ldr: {lo: skinned low-detail soldier (what the game shows at the default zoom), hi: close-zoom soldier where exported}}, "extra": rigid meshes that belong to the unit (mortar tube...). Every soldier file is root "soldier" > "pose" (the clips move it: hip height, prone, death) > skeleton + one mesh "soldier_mesh". The clips live in "animFile" (same node paths: copy its AnimationLibrary).

clips.walk: one stride, loop; play at speed/cycleDist cycles per second
clips.run: the jog every infantry unit uses at full speed, loop
clips.crouch: stand to crouch, hold the last frame
clips.die: tips over backwards; the game removes the body after 6 s
clips.fire: none in the game: firing is a muzzle flash and tracer only

partsDoc.body: the model itself (the game bobs / banks it)
partsDoc.turret: turned toward the target (weapon mount, launcher rack)
partsDoc.gun: building gun, turned toward the target
partsDoc.glow: jet exhaust plumes (runtime shader; positions under runtime)
partsDoc.cargo: supply-truck load, shown only when loaded
partsDoc.crane: dozer arm / EW dish: swings or spins about Y
partsDoc.flag: cloth takes the team colour / nation flag
partsDoc.tring: team-colour ring under the unit (runtime decal)

_meta.runtime: things the game adds at run time that a glb cannot carry (the weathering/camouflage shader is weather() in js-final:src/11-models.js lines 206-251; mat.wx = its wear amount, mat.camo.freq = its camouflage frequency, mat.wall + mat.trim = painted wall bands on buildings), listed per look: {t:"decal",k:"ringV|ringS"} team-colour ring (colour = team), "blob" soft contact shadow, "lamp" headlight pool at night; "shaderMesh" (jet exhaust plume, additive); "lines" (scaffold); "hiddenNode" (shown later by the game: damage, night lights); material flags camo{a,b,c,pattern,scale} = procedural camouflage painted by the weathering shader over the base colour, look = surface class of the detail shader (metal/canvas/concrete/glass...), refl = sky reflection, wake = water wake/air haze class.
_meta.teamColour: models were painted with the nation's own default team colour (_nation.color). The game mixes the team colour only faintly into the paint (6% or less on nation-painted vehicles, aircraft and soldiers; 16% on unpainted models, 10% on generic infantry); teams are told apart by the ring decal under each unit and the flags.
_meta.wrecks: a destroyed vehicle is the same model with a burnt material (dark, heat glow fading) tilted a few degrees; buildings leave one of the three _map.rubble heaps scaled to the footprint
_meta.soldiersAtRuntime: the JS game draws all soldiers of one look in one instanced batch with a bone texture (SOLB) and swaps to the low-detail mesh beyond camera distance 480; the default battle camera (560) shows the low-detail mesh.
